verdicts.claim: The unassisted baseline achieves a 44.2% win rate by villagers, lower than random.
verdicts.evidence_quote: the vanilla baseline (Group A) winning at a rate of 44.2% that is lower than random
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; Table 2 confirms Group A win rate 44.2%.

verdicts.claim: Combining MaKTO-Proxy and DBN increases win rate to 68.8%.
verdicts.evidence_quote: Group E (MaKTO + DBN, 68.8%) had an increase in win-rate of approximately 24.6 percentage points
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; Table 2 confirms Group E win rate 68.8%.

verdicts.claim: Vote accuracy rises monotonically from 35.5% to 66.6%.
verdicts.evidence_quote: The percent accuracy of the vote rose monotonically (35.5% A, 66.6% F)
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; Table 2 vote accuracy values confirm monotonic rise.

verdicts.claim: Group F has the highest vote accuracy but the shortest survival.
verdicts.evidence_quote: Group F was the poorest in terms of mean survival (2.33 rounds) but a win rate was slightly lower than E
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; Table 2 confirms Group F vote accuracy 66.6% (highest) and survival 2.33 (shortest).

verdicts.claim: DBN and MaKTO have orthogonal and additive effects.
verdicts.evidence_quote: indicative of the two modules acting in orthogonal directions and having additive effects as opposed to redundant
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; paper notes combined gain ~24.6 pp similar to sum of independent gains (~20 pp).

verdicts.claim: DTR contributes more vote accuracy in the presence of MaKTO.
verdicts.evidence_quote: it contributes +3.4 pp in the absence of MaKTO (C→D) and +7.3 pp in the presence of MaKTO (E→F)
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; paper explicitly states positive interaction between the two variables.

verdicts.evidence_quote: Since round 2, the groups of DBNs (C through F) decline more rapidly and F becomes less than 0.05 by round 3
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; DBN groups decline more rapidly than A/B.

verdicts.evidence_quote: The Brier Score of the terminals and ideal BCR (1.63 rounds) are lowest when 0.3 is set
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; sensitivity analysis under Configuration C (500 games each).

verdicts.claim: Werewolf utterances have higher DTR density peaks.
verdicts.evidence_quote: There is a higher density peak of werewolves, which is in line with the fact that deception is a complex cognitive processing
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; Figure 9 DTR distributions by role.

verdicts.claim: The full-module configuration leads to early elimination of the target agent.
verdicts.evidence_quote: the combination of the full-module results in the identification efficiency so high that the target agent shows an apparent information advantage in the course of discussion that forces the opponent to kill it early
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; survival rounds 2.33 vs 2.73 support the mechanism.

verdicts.claim: The capability-survival conflict is analogous to the handicap principle.
verdicts.evidence_quote: This structurally corresponds to the signaling theory and the handicap principle
verdicts.note: Quote found verbatim; paper discusses Spence signaling theory and Zahavi handicap principle.

limitations.issue: Small sample sizes / limited game counts for some analyses
limitations.why: Alpha sensitivity analysis uses only 500 games per condition (Configuration C), and the six main configurations appear to rely on a limited number of games; statistical significance is not reported.
Win-rate and vote-accuracy differences (e.g., 68.8% vs 68.2% between E and F) are reported without confidence intervals or significance tests, so some differences may not be robust.

limitations.issue: Overlap in DTR distributions limits discriminability
limitations.why: The paper itself notes 'a large amount of overlap, which restricts complete discriminability' between werewolf and villager DTR distributions, tempering the strength of the DTR signal.
The orthogonal/additive claim rests on ~24.6 pp vs ~20 pp sum of independent gains, which is approximate and not exact; the paper acknowledges this is 'approximately' additive.

overall_assessment: All 11 claims are supported by the quoted evidence and surrounding context. The Reader's claims accurately reflect the paper's reported results, including win rates, vote accuracy, survival, module interactions, Brier Score convergence, alpha sensitivity, DTR density, and the discussion of the handicap principle. The main caveats are methodological: limited game counts, absence of statistical significance testing, and the approximate nature of the additivity claim.
